raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

SGLang's ROCm path primarily targets AMD Instinct GPUs. RDNA4 `gfx1201`
devices such as the Radeon AI PRO R9700 need architecture-specific build
settings and backend selection to run supported dense and MoE workloads.

This PR adds experimental single-GPU `gfx1201` inference support for BF16/FP16,
online FP8 quantization, Triton BF16/FP8 MoE, and native MXFP4 GPT-OSS models.

## Modifications

- Add `gfx1201` detection and ROCm kernel build configuration with wave32 and
  OCP E4M3 FP8 support.
- Default MHA and MLA attention to Triton on `gfx1201` and keep unsupported
  AITER paths disabled.
- Enable online FP8 dense inference and BF16/FP8 Triton fused MoE kernels.
- Enable native GPT-OSS MXFP4 inference through `triton_kernels`, including
  compatibility with both the legacy `routing_data` and current
  `x_ragged_metadata` matmul APIs.
- Add wave32-compatible MoE TopK handling, architecture guards, focused CPU and
  AMD GPU regression tests, and `gfx1201` documentation.

The `gfx1201` path is intentionally limited to one GPU. Custom all-reduce,
tensor/expert parallelism, AITER, Quark MXFP4, and other untested quantization
formats remain unsupported.

## Accuracy Tests

Validated on an AMD Radeon AI PRO R9700 (`gfx1201`) with ROCm 7.2:

- PR-scope pre-commit hooks: passed.
- Focused CPU/configuration regressions: 7 passed, including 2 subtests.
- The complete gfx1201 and Quark configuration test files passed all 12 tests,
  including 2 subtests.
- Registered `gfx1201` AMD tests: 5 passed using the current pinned
  `triton_kernels` API. These cover TopK softmax/sigmoid, BF16 and FP8 fused
  MoE, FP8 scaled matmul, MXFP4 matmul, and MXFP4 MoE routing against a
  dequantized BF16 reference.
- The same 5 registered tests passed with the legacy `matmul_ogs` API.
- Compiled `sgl-kernel` AOT probes passed for TopK softmax/sigmoid,
  `silu_and_mul`, and MoE block alignment.
- A clean `sgl-kernel` snapshot from the final PR HEAD built and packaged as a
  gfx1201-only wheel with zero unsupported CUDA calls; the isolated wheel
  install passed the same AOT probes.
- The complete compiled `sgl-kernel` MoE TopK softmax/sigmoid parameter matrix
  passed all 1518 cases on `gfx1201`.
- 270 routing compatibility cases passed.
- Real `sglang.Engine` smoke tests passed for Qwen3-0.6B BF16, Qwen3-0.6B
  online FP8, and GPT-OSS-20B native MXFP4. Each generated 16 tokens; GPT-OSS
  loaded 13.09 GB of weights and selected `moe_runner_backend=triton_kernel`.
  BF16 and online FP8 were repeated from the final PR HEAD with the isolated
  wheel and no explicit attention override; both automatically selected
  `attention_backend=triton` and completed successfully.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No performance improvement is claimed. The Engine runs above are functional
validation, not benchmarks.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

@@ -3,6 +3,24 @@ title: "AMD GPUs"
 ---
 This document describes how to run SGLang on AMD GPUs. If you encounter issues or have questions, please [open an issue](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues).
 
+## Supported architectures
+
+SGLang supports AMD Instinct `gfx942` and `gfx950` GPUs. Experimental single-GPU
+support is also available for RDNA4 `gfx1201` GPUs such as Radeon AI PRO R9700
+and Radeon RX 9070 series cards.
+
+The initial `gfx1201` support includes BF16/FP16 dense models, FP8 online
+quantization for dense models, single-GPU BF16/FP8 Triton MoE, and single-GPU
+GPT-OSS inference with its native MXFP4 checkpoint. Use the Triton attention
+backend. Other quantization formats, custom all-reduce, and multi-GPU serving
+are not yet supported on this architecture. Keep AITER disabled on gfx1201.
+
+Use ROCm 7.2 or later. AMD's [Radeon PyTorch installation guide](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/projects/radeon-ryzen/en/latest/docs/install/installrad/native_linux/install-pytorch.html)
+lists the supported operating systems and official PyTorch containers. AMD's
+[GPU architecture specifications](https://rocm.docs.amd.com/en/latest/reference/gpu-arch-specs.html)
+identify `gfx1201` as an RDNA4 target with 32-or-64-lane wavefront support and
+128 KiB of LDS.
+
 ## System Configuration
 
 When using AMD GPUs (such as MI300X), certain system-level optimizations help ensure stable performance. Here we take MI300X as an example. AMD provides official documentation for MI300X optimization and system tuning:
@@ -59,6 +77,70 @@ rm -rf python/pyproject.toml && mv python/pyproject_other.toml python/pyproject.
 pip install -e "python[all_hip]"
 ```
 
+For an experimental `gfx1201` source build, compile a single-architecture
+kernel and leave the full Aiter backend disabled:
+
+```bash Command
+export AMDGPU_TARGET=gfx1201
+export PYTORCH_ROCM_ARCH=gfx1201
+export GPU_ARCHS=gfx1201
+export SGLANG_USE_AITER=0
+
+cd sgl-kernel
+python setup_rocm.py install
+cd ..
+
+# SGLang currently uses the matmul_ogs API from this triton_kernels revision.
+python -m pip install --no-deps \
+    "git+https://github.com/triton-lang/triton.git@4a24bf0b19a027ec0833b31cbc9ac29add7b17af#subdirectory=python/triton_kernels"
+
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attention-backend triton \
+    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": false}' \
+    --tp 1
+```
+
+The single-threaded loader avoids long host-to-device copy stalls observed with
+parallel checkpoint loading on RDNA4. It does not affect inference after the
+model is loaded. Large checkpoints can still spend several minutes registering
+host memory with ROCm before the load-complete message appears.
+
+FP8 online quantization uses PyTorch/hipBLASLt and does not require AITER:
+
+```bash Command
+python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B \
+    --quantization fp8 \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attention-backend triton \
+    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": false}' \
+    --tp 1
+```
+
+MXFP4 support on `gfx1201` is limited to the native MXFP4 GPT-OSS checkpoint,
+one GPU, and the `triton_kernel` MoE runner. SGLang selects that runner
+automatically when `--moe-runner-backend auto` is used:
+
+```bash Command
+SGLANG_USE_AITER=0 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
+    --model-path openai/gpt-oss-20b \
+    --dtype bfloat16 \
+    --attention-backend triton \
+    --moe-runner-backend auto \
+    --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": false}' \
+    --tp 1
+```
+
+The `gfx1201` path keeps the checkpoint's canonical MXFP4 value and scale
+layouts. It does not use the CDNA4 HBM swizzle. AITER/Quark MXFP4, expert
+parallelism, and tensor parallelism are not supported on this path.
+
+Do not combine `gfx1201` with CDNA targets in the same `sgl-kernel` build. CDNA
+and RDNA resolve warp-size-dependent code differently, and some host-side launch
+calculations are not yet safe in a mixed-architecture binary.
+
 ### Install Using Docker (Recommended)
 
 The docker images are available on Docker Hub at [lmsysorg/sglang](https://hub.docker.com/r/lmsysorg/sglang/tags), built from [rocm.Dockerfile](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/docker).

+    def test_moe_topk(self):
+        from sglang.kernels.ops.moe import topk_softmax
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import fused_topk
+
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        for num_experts in (4, 6):
+            logits = torch.randn(4, num_experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            actual_weights = torch.empty(4, 2, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
+            actual_ids = torch.empty(4, 2, device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
+
+            topk_softmax(actual_weights, actual_ids, logits)
+            expected_weights, expected_ids = torch.softmax(logits.float(), dim=-1).topk(
+                2, dim=-1
+            )
+
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                actual_weights, expected_weights, atol=1e-6, rtol=1e-5
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual_ids, expected_ids.to(torch.int32))
+
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(4, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        for num_experts in (8, 6):
+            logits = torch.randn(4, num_experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+            actual_weights, actual_ids = fused_topk(
+                hidden_states,
+                logits,
+                topk=2,
+                renormalize=True,
+                scoring_func="sigmoid",
+            )
+            expected_weights, expected_ids = torch.sigmoid(logits.float()).topk(
+                2, dim=-1
+            )
+            expected_weights /= expected_weights.sum(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                actual_weights, expected_weights, atol=1e-3, rtol=1e-3
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(actual_ids, expected_ids.to(torch.int32))
+
+    def test_bf16_and_fp8_fused_moe(self):
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.moe_runner.triton_utils.fused_moe import (
+            fused_moe,
+        )
+        from sglang.srt.layers.moe.topk import TopKConfig, select_experts
+        from sglang.srt.server_args import (
+            ServerArgs,
+            set_global_server_args_for_scheduler,
+        )
+
+        set_global_server_args_for_scheduler(ServerArgs(model_path="dummy"))
+        torch.manual_seed(1)
+        tokens, experts, hidden_size, intermediate_size, top_k = 4, 4, 256, 128, 2
+        hidden_states = torch.randn(
+            tokens, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16
+        )
+        logits = torch.randn(tokens, experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        w13_bf16 = (
+            torch.randn(
+                experts,
+                2 * intermediate_size,
+                hidden_size,
+                device="cuda",
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            )
+            * 0.01
+        )
+        w2_bf16 = (
+            torch.randn(
+                experts,
+                hidden_size,
+                intermediate_size,
+                device="cuda",
+                dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+            )
+            * 0.01
+        )
+        topk_output = select_experts(
+            hidden_states=hidden_states,
+            router_logits=logits,
+            topk_config=TopKConfig(top_k=top_k, renormalize=False),
+        )
+
+        fp8_modes = (
+            (False, False, None, None, None),
+            (
+                True,
+                False,
+                torch.ones(experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+                torch.ones(experts, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+                None,
+            ),
+            (
+                True,
+                True,
+                torch.ones(
+                    experts,
+                    2 * intermediate_size,
+                    device="cuda",
+                    dtype=torch.float32,
+                ),
+                torch.ones(experts, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+                None,
+            ),
+            (
+                True,
+                False,
+                torch.ones(experts, 2, 2, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+                torch.ones(experts, 2, 1, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+                [128, 128],
+            ),
+        )
+        for use_fp8, per_channel_quant, w13_scale, w2_scale, block_shape in fp8_modes:
+            w13 = w13_bf16.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) if use_fp8 else w13_bf16
+            w2 = w2_bf16.to(torch.float8_e4m3fn) if use_fp8 else w2_bf16
+
+            actual = fused_moe(

+                w13,
+                w2,
+                topk_output,
+                use_fp8_w8a8=use_fp8,
+                per_channel_quant=per_channel_quant,
+                w1_scale=w13_scale,
+                w2_scale=w2_scale,
+                block_shape=block_shape,

+                    expert_id = int(topk_ids[token_id, route_id])
+                    gate_up = (
+                        hidden_states[token_id] @ w13[expert_id].to(torch.bfloat16).t()
+                    )
+                    gate, up = gate_up.chunk(2)
+                    expert_output = (torch.nn.functional.silu(gate) * up) @ w2[
+                        expert_id
+                    ].to(torch.bfloat16).t()
+                    expected[token_id] += (
+                        expert_output * topk_weights[token_id, route_id]
+                    )
+
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                actual.float(), expected.float(), atol=0.35, rtol=0.08
+            )

+    def test_fp8_scaled_mm(self):
+        torch.manual_seed(1)
+        x = torch.randn(16, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        weight = torch.randn(256, 256, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+        x_scale = x.float().abs().max().clamp_min(1e-12) / 448.0
+        weight_scale = weight.float().abs().max().clamp_min(1e-12) / 448.0
+        x_fp8 = (x.float() / x_scale).clamp(-448, 448).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        weight_fp8 = (
+            (weight.float() / weight_scale).clamp(-448, 448).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
+        )
+
+        actual = torch._scaled_mm(
+            x_fp8,
+            weight_fp8.t(),
+            scale_a=x_scale.reshape(1),
+            scale_b=weight_scale.reshape(1),
+            out_dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        if isinstance(actual, tuple):
+            actual = actual[0]
+        expected = (x_fp8.float() * x_scale) @ (weight_fp8.float() * weight_scale).t()
+        torch.testing.assert_close(actual.float(), expected, atol=0.2, rtol=0.03)

+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            new_api_gather_indx.src_indx,
+            torch.div(gather_indx.src_indx, 2, rounding_mode="trunc"),
+        )
+        torch.testing.assert_close(new_api_gather_indx.dst_indx, gather_indx.dst_indx)
+
+        w13 = torch.randn(
+            experts,
+            2 * intermediate_size,
+            hidden_size,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        w2 = torch.randn(
+            experts,
+            hidden_size,
+            intermediate_size,
+            device="cuda",
+            dtype=torch.bfloat16,
+        )
+        w13_fp4, w13_scale_raw = downcast_to_mxfp_torch(w13, torch.uint8, axis=-1)
+        w2_fp4, w2_scale_raw = downcast_to_mxfp_torch(w2, torch.uint8, axis=-1)
+        w13_wrapped, w13_flex, w13_scale = _swizzle_mxfp4(
+            w13_fp4, w13_scale_raw, num_warps=8, use_hbm_swizzle=False
+        )
+        w2_wrapped, w2_flex, w2_scale = _swizzle_mxfp4(
+            w2_fp4, w2_scale_raw, num_warps=8, use_hbm_swizzle=False
+        )
+
+        actual = triton_kernel_fused_experts_with_bias(
+            hidden_states=hidden_states,
+            w1=w13_wrapped,
+            w1_pcg=PrecisionConfig(
+                weight_scale=w13_scale, flex_ctx=FlexCtx(rhs_data=w13_flex)
+            ),
+            b1=torch.zeros(
+                experts, 2 * intermediate_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32
+            ),
+            w2=w2_wrapped,
+            w2_pcg=PrecisionConfig(
+                weight_scale=w2_scale, flex_ctx=FlexCtx(rhs_data=w2_flex)
+            ),
+            b2=torch.zeros(experts, hidden_size, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32),
+            routing_data=routing_data,
+            gather_indx=gather_indx,
+            scatter_indx=scatter_indx,
+            gemm1_alpha=1.702,
+            gemm1_clamp_limit=7.0,
+        )
+
+        self.assertEqual(actual.shape, hidden_states.shape)
+        w13_dequant = upcast_from_mxfp_torch(
+            w13_fp4, w13_scale_raw, target_dtype=torch.bfloat16, axis=-1
+        )
+        w2_dequant = upcast_from_mxfp_torch(
+            w2_fp4, w2_scale_raw, target_dtype=torch.bfloat16, axis=-1
+        )
+        topk_logits, topk_ids = logits.topk(2, dim=-1)
+        topk_weights = torch.softmax(topk_logits, dim=-1)
+        expected = torch.zeros_like(hidden_states, dtype=torch.float32)
+        for token_id in range(tokens):
+            for route_id in range(2):
+                expert_id = int(topk_ids[token_id, route_id])
+                gate_up = (
+                    hidden_states[token_id].float() @ w13_dequant[expert_id].float().t()
+                )
+                gate = gate_up[::2].clamp(max=7.0)
+                linear = gate_up[1::2].clamp(min=-7.0, max=7.0)
+                activated = gate * torch.sigmoid(1.702 * gate) * (linear + 1)
+                expert_output = activated @ w2_dequant[expert_id].float().t()
+                expected[token_id] += expert_output * topk_weights[token_id, route_id]
+
+        torch.testing.assert_close(
+            actual.float(),
+            expected,
+            atol=2.0,
+            rtol=0.05,
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+import unittest

+

+from sglang.srt.server_args import ServerArgs

+class TestGfx1201QuantizationSupport(unittest.TestCase):
+    def test_default_attention_backend_is_triton(self):
+        model_config = SimpleNamespace(
+            hf_config=SimpleNamespace(architectures=["Qwen3ForCausalLM"])
+        )
+        with (
+            patch.object(
+                server_args_module.current_platform,
+                "is_out_of_tree",
+                return_value=False,
+            ),
+            patch.object(
+                server_args_module, "is_hopper_with_cuda_12_3", return_value=False
+            ),
+            patch.object(server_args_module, "is_sm100_supported", return_value=False),
+            patch.object(server_args_module, "is_gfx1201_supported", return_value=True),
+        ):
+            for use_mla_backend in (False, True):
+                with self.subTest(use_mla_backend=use_mla_backend):
+                    self.assertEqual(
+                        ServerArgs._get_default_attn_backend(
+                            SimpleNamespace(), use_mla_backend, model_config
+                        ),
+                        "triton",
+                    )
+
+    def test_triton_kernels_requires_compatible_matmul_api(self):
+        def find_spec_without_matmul_ogs(module):
+            return None if module == "triton_kernels.matmul_ogs" else object()
+
+        common.is_triton_kernels_available.cache_clear()
+        self.addCleanup(common.is_triton_kernels_available.cache_clear)
+        with patch.object(
+            common.importlib.util,
+            "find_spec",
+            side_effect=find_spec_without_matmul_ogs,
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(common.is_triton_kernels_available())
+
+    def test_mxfp4_requires_triton_kernels(self):
+        props = SimpleNamespace(gcnArchName="gfx1201")
+        with (
+            patch.object(common.torch.version, "hip", "7.2"),
+            patch.object(
+                common.torch.cuda, "get_device_properties", return_value=props
+            ),
+            patch.object(common, "is_triton_kernels_available", return_value=False),
+        ):
+            self.assertFalse(common.mxfp_supported())
+
+        with (
+            patch.object(common.torch.version, "hip", "7.2"),
+            patch.object(
+                common.torch.cuda, "get_device_properties", return_value=props
+            ),
+            patch.object(common, "is_triton_kernels_available", return_value=True),
+        ):
+            self.assertTrue(common.mxfp_supported())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

The PR-author `/tag-and-rerun-ci extra` command was accepted, but the slash-command handler reported `can_tag_run_ci_label is false`; all rerun attempts therefore stopped at the unchanged label gate (`Missing required label run-ci`) without executing tests.
